issue_definition: A dwc:MaterialEntity that is geological in nature.
issue_examples: a specific mineral; a specific rock; a specific ore
notes: New class created during the review (subtype of dwc:MaterialEntity) to hold geology-only properties. Not yet in the repo term list; add it.
Existing DwC class; listed in the repo for context only (no issue needed).

issue_definition: The qualitative or quantitative abundance of a dwc:MaterialEntity with respect to another dwc:MaterialEntity of which it is a part.
issue_usage_notes: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as http://resource.geosciml.org/classifier/cgi/proportionterm
issue_examples: 20%; minor; dominant
repo_definition: The qualitative or quantitative abundance of a specimen part relative to its parent compound specimen.

issue_definition: A category that best matches the nature of the relationship between a dwc:MaterialEntity and another dwc:MaterialEntity of which it is a part.
issue_usage_notes: Roles depend on both the part and the parent object. For instance, a rock (material category) within the parent specimen serves as a clast and depends on both the specimen part and the parent specimen for its existence. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as IUGS CGI Compound Material Consituent Part, http://resource.geosciml.org/classifier/cgi/compoundmaterialconstituentpartrole
issue_examples: matrix; groundmass; phenocryst; xenolith; vein
repo_definition: Specifies the relationship between a specimen part and its parent compound specimen.

issue_definition: Remarks on the physical characteristics of a dwc:MaterialEntity, particularly those that distinguish it from otherwise similar dwc:MaterialEntities.
issue_examples: Showpiece; Historically valuable; Extraordinary composition; Two generations of quartz
repo_definition: Comments or notes about the specimen (physical object) especially those that distinguish the specimen from similar materials in a collection.
notes: #962 mineralDescription was merged into this term.

issue_definition: The verbatim original representation of the mass of a dwc:MaterialEntity, including original units of measurement.
repo_definition: The original reported verbatim mass includes original units of measurement

issue_definition: Mass of a dwc:MaterialEntity, measured in grams.
repo_definition: Mass of specimen measured in grams

issue_definition: The designation of a geological material by a linguistic expression including both informal (verbatim) and formal (classifications) types.
repo_definition: The designation of a geological material by a linguistic expression including both informal (verbatim) and formal (classifications) types.
notes: Class withdrawn; the repo still lists GeoName as a class.

issue_definition: A list (concatenated and separated) of mineral or lithotaxon names for a dwc:GeologicalMaterial.
issue_usage_notes: May includes both informal (e.g., variety, synonym) and formal (classification) names. The first name in the list should be considered the preferred name. Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
issue_examples: quartz | smoky quartz; muscovite; garnet group
repo_definition: A human-readable lexical label assigned to a geological material includes both informal (e.g., variety, synonym) and formal (classification) forms.
notes: Renamed to plural list form during review; the repo still uses the singular geologicalMaterialName.

issue_definition: An identifier for a mineral or lithotaxon name for a dwc:GeologicalMaterial. May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.
issue_usage_notes: Recommended best practice is to use a persistent, globally unique identifier.
issue_examples: https://geospecimens.org/api/v1/catalog/resource/mineral-name/ba673bdf-7228-11f0-a057-52f8e1bb0628
repo_definition: An identifier for the set of dwc:GeoName information. May be a globally unique identifier or a dataset-specific identifier.
notes: The issue title says geologicalMaterialNameID but the proposal body says geologicMaterialNameID; the repo uses geologicalMaterialNameID. Reconcile the spelling in the issue body.

issue_definition: A list (concatenated and separated) of the types of names provided in dwc:geologicalMaterialNames.
issue_usage_notes: If this term is populated, it should have an equal number of items in the list as for the list in dwc:geologicalMaterialNames and the types should have the same order as the names to which they refer. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary for the values in a list (e.g., https://kos.geospecimens.org/def/geological-specimen-name-type). See Gavryliv (2023), https://doi.org/10.1180/mgm.2023.23, for a detailed breakdown of informal, alternate names.
issue_examples: species | variety; species; group; synonym; classification; historical
repo_definition: A term belonging to a categorization scheme for organizing geological material names based on usage and concept lineage.
notes: Renamed to plural list form during review; the repo still uses the singular geologicalMaterialNameType.

repo_definition: Language of the name
notes: In the repo list (dcterms namespace) but no DwC issue was filed. Not part of the review.

issue_definition: A reference to the classification system in which an authoritative name or formal classification belongs.
issue_usage_notes: Recommended best practice is to provide a formal citation or IRI. This term should not be confused with dwc:namePublishedIn as a classification system is not equivalent to a publication in which a taxon is first described. This term should not be confused with dwc:nameAccordingTo as a classification system is not equivalent to a publication or other source in which a specific taxon concept circumscription is defined or implied. This term should not be confused with dwc:nomenclaturalCode as a classification system is not equivalent to code of nomenclature, which states the rules for naming rather than an organized source of names.
issue_examples: Strunz, H., Nickel, E.H. (2001): Strunz Mineralogical Tables. Chemical-Structural Mineral Classification System. 9th edition. E. Schweizerbart’sche Verlagsbuchhandlung, Stuttgart, ix + 870 p. (ISBN 3-510-65188-X); Gaines, R.V., Skinner, H.C.W., Foord, E.E., Mason, B., Rosenzweig, A. (1997): Dana's New Mineralogy: The System of Mineralogy of James Dwight Dana and Edward Salisbury Dana. 8th edition. John Wiley & Sons, New York, xlv + 1819 p. (ISBN 0-471-19310-0).; https://kos.geospecimens.org/vocab/meteorite-classification; Mammal Diversity Database. (2026). Mammal Diversity Database (Version 2.5) [Data set]. [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/10595931). https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17033774; Index Fungorum. (2026). Index Fungorum electronic database. Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew. Retrieved August 17, 2026, from indexfungorum.org.
repo_definition: A reference to the classification system in which an authoritative name or formal classification belongs, provided as formal citations or URI to an external resource.
notes: Re-homed from GeoName to dwc:Identification.

issue_definition: A list (concatenated and separated) of codes that each identifies a name from a classification system applied to a dwc:GeologicalMaterial.
issue_usage_notes: Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
issue_examples: 71.02.02a.01 ("muscovite" in the Dana classification system); 9.AD.25 ("garnet group" in the Nickel-Strunz classification system); 75.01.03.01 | 4.DA.05 ("quartz" the Dana classification system and "quartz group" in the Nickel-Strunz classification system)
repo_definition: Alphanumeric pattern that adheres to a defined encoding scheme that identifies a particular term in a classification scheme.
notes: #946 classificationCode was closed as a duplicate of #937; the repo still uses the singular classificationCode.

issue_definition: Analytical technique utilized to confirm the identity of a geological material.
issue_usage_notes: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as Analytical methods for geochemistry and cosmochemistry (https://w3id.org/geochem/1.0/analyticalmethod/method).
issue_examples: X-ray Diffraction Raman Spectroscopy
repo_definition: Analytical technique utilized to confirm the identity of a geological material.

issue_definition: A string representing the classification as it appeared in the original record.
issue_usage_notes: This term is meant to allow the capture of an unaltered original classification/identification/determination, including identification qualifiers, hybrid formulas, uncertainties, etc. This term is meant to be used in addition to dwc:geologicalMaterialName or dwc:scientificName (and dwc:identificationQualifier etc.), not instead of it.
issue_examples: Peromyscus sp.; Ministrymon sp. nov. 1; Anser anser × Branta canadensis; Pachyporidae?; Potentilla × pantotricha Soják; Aconitum pilipes × A. variegatum; Lepomis auritus x cyanellus
notes: Change to an existing DwC term (definition broadened from 'taxonomic identification' to 'classification'). Not in the repo term list.

issue_usage_notes: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as https://kos.geospecimens.org/vocab/hazard-type
issue_examples: carcinogen; skin irritant; radioactive; toxic
repo_definition: A term that belongs to a hazard classification scheme based on a set of unique characteristics and negative health outcomes.

issue_examples: asbestos; slightly radioactive; requires skin protection

issue_definition: Processes, protocols, and techniques established for the purpose of the protection and preservation of a mineral or specimen.
issue_usage_notes: Conservation terms are applied at the specimen level to simplify usage. If conservation is associated with a specific part of a compound specimen, then that should be declared in the description.
repo_definition: Processes, protocols, and techniques established for the purpose of the protection and preservation of a mineral or specimen.
notes: Class withdrawn; the repo still lists Conservation as a class.

issue_definition: Description of any processes or curatorial actions taken specifically to mitigate damage to a dwc:MaterialEntity.
issue_usage_notes: Includes both proactive and reactive actions.

issue_definition: A description of the procedures required to preserve and protect a dwc:MaterialEntity during handling.
issue_examples: handle with gloves; not to be taken out of storage medium; avoid contact with direct sunlight
repo_definition: A summary of the procedural requirements employed to preserve and protect the specimen during physical interaction.

issue_definition: A general description of any physical changes to a dwc:MaterialEntity that have negatively affected its value.
issue_usage_notes: See Royce, K., Baars, C., & Viles, H. (2021). Defining Damage and Susceptibility, with Implications for Mineral Specimens and Objects: Introducing the Mineral Susceptibility Database. Studies in Conservation, 68(3), 298-317. https://doi.org/10.1080/00393630.2021.2015947
issue_examples: Due to oxidation and hydration of the pyrite in the coal, the sample has largely decayed to a coal powder with some larger coal pieces | Some terminations broken off | Attached label not legible (or torn, or covered)
repo_definition: A general description of any material changes to a specimen which is perceived to have negatively affected an item's value-defining aspects.

issue_definition: A list (concatenated and separated) of resources associated with the reported measured chemistry described specifically enough to allow anyone in the future to use the same resources.
issue_usage_notes: Recommended best practice is to use full bibliographic citations, global unique identifiers, or resolvable and persistent IRIs. See the broader concept http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/associatedReferences
issue_examples: Novak, G. A., & Gibbs, G. V. (1971). The crystal chemistry of the silicate garnets. American Mineralogist: Journal of Earth and Planetary Materials, 56(5-6), 791-825.
repo_definition: A list (concatenated and separated) of resources associated with the reported measured chemistry described specifically enough to allow anyone in the future to use the same resources.

issue_definition: A technique used to determine the chemical composition or crystallography of a mineral.
issue_usage_notes: Acronyms should be avoided even for widely recognized annotations. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as https://vocabs.ardc.edu.au/viewById/650
issue_examples: Wet Chemistry; X-ray fluorescence; Electron probe microanalysis; Scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy; X-ray diffraction
repo_definition: The technique utilized to determine the chemical composition or crystallography of a mineral.

issue_definition: An extensive named region with similar geologic history, structural, petrographic, or physiographic features throughout in which the GeologicalContext was located.
issue_examples: Northwest Province; Surprise Paleovalley; Basin and Range; Coastal Plain; Piedmont; Blue Ridge
repo_definition: Extensive named region with a similar geologic history throughout or similar structural, petrographic, or physiographic features in which the dwc:Location occurs

issue_definition: A geologic unit that lacks stratification, is primarily comprised of intrusive, deformed, and/or metamorphosed rock, and is characterized by irregularly mixed lithology or highly complicated structural relations.
issue_usage_notes: Due to the unstructured nature of complexes, both named units and lithological descriptive terms are acceptable values.
issue_examples: Catalina Core Complex; injection complex; New England Plutonic Suite; Sierra Nevada batholith
repo_definition: Geologic unit that lacks stratification, primarily comprised of intrusive, deformed, and/or metamorphosed rock, and characterized by irregularly mixed lithology or highly complicated structural relations.

issue_definition: A name of an identifiable event during which one or more geologic processes acted to create or modify one or more dwc:GeologicalMaterials.
issue_examples: Sevier orogeny; Alleghanian orogeny; Alpine orogeny; Variscan orogeny; Vredefort impact
repo_definition: An identifiable event during which one or more geological processes associated with the formation of a geological specimen or act to modify an existing geological specimen.

issue_definition: A list (concatenated and separated) of minerals in a dwc:GeologicalMaterial, ordered in a manner that illustrates the relative timing of mineral formation.
issue_usage_notes: The list should only contain minerals that belong to a readily identifiable sequence of formation. Therefore, a list may contain a subset of the minerals in a specimen. Minerals that formed in-situ with one another are separated by a plus. Minerals that formed in the sequence are separated by a greater than (' > ') symbol.
issue_examples: Sphalerite > Quartz > Pyrite; Calcite > Quartz > Sphalerite > Pyrite
repo_definition: A list of minerals in a specimen ordered in a manner that illustrates the relative timing of mineral formation within a specimen.

issue_definition: The combination of all tectonic unit names for the rock from which the dwc:MaterialEntity was collected.
issue_usage_notes: Recommended best practice is to use an authoritative tectonic unit lexicon such as the Tectonic Map of Switzerland (TK500).
issue_examples: Upper Helvetic; Wildhorn Nappe Complex; Sublage Nappe
repo_definition: The combination of all tectonic unit names for the rock from which the dwc:MaterialEntity was collected.

issue_definition: The type of naturally occurring or anthropogenic physical feature from which a dwc:MaterialEntity was sampled.
issue_usage_notes: A sampled feature has a type and an optional name that distinguishes the feature from similar entities. Sampled features can be anthropogenic (roadcut, borehole) or naturally occurring (outcrop). Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.
issue_examples: float; mine dump; mine/quarry pit; outcrop; erratic boulder
repo_definition: The type of physical feature, both naturally occurring and anthropogenic in origin, sampled during a sampling event (dwc:Event) at a dwc:Location
notes: Renamed from sampledFeature and moved to MaterialEntity during review; the repo still uses sampledFeature under Location.

issue_definition: The full, unabbreviated name of a geographic location not otherwise categorized by a dcterms:Location property that is naturally occurring or anthropogenic in origin within a historical, administrative, or cultural context in which a dcterms:Location occurs.
issue_usage_notes: Recommended best practice is to leave this field blank if the dcterms:Location spans multiple entities or may be in multiple possible entities that meet the term definition. For named places represented as URIs or global unique identifiers, please use dwc:locationID.
issue_examples: 11th Level, Bergwerksglücker Lode, Wiemannsbucht Mine; Craigleith Quarry; Red Cloud Mine; NEON Niwot Ridge Mountain Research Station (NIWO); Hagerman Fossil Beds; Mauna Kea
repo_definition: The full, unabbreviated name of a geographic location not otherwise categorized by a dwc:Location property that is naturally occurring or anthropogenic in origin within a historical, administrative, or cultural context in which dcterms:Location occurs.

issue_usage_notes: Recommended best practice is to follow the TDWG Boolean Controlled Vocabulary http://rs.tdwg.org/tag/doc/boolean/.
issue_examples: true; false
notes: Proposed but not in the repo term list; still unresolved in review.
